_help._note: Help text shown in the customer platform's setup wizard. It is never read by the bot: it exists so a shop owner can fill a field in without guessing.
_help.business.name: Exactly as customers know it. 'Al-Madina Bakers', not 'my bakery business'.
_help.business.type: What kind of business this is. The wizard sets it from the template you pick.
_help.business.city: The city customers collect from or get delivery in. Used for timing and delivery answers.
_help.business.hours: Opening hours in plain words, e.g. 'Daily 12:00-23:00, closed Tuesdays'. The assistant quotes this instead of guessing.
_help.business.languages: Comma separated, e.g. English, Urdu. The assistant replies in the language the customer writes in.
_help.business.tone: How it should sound, e.g. 'warm and brief' or 'formal English'. Short is better.
_help.catalog: One item per line: name | price | note. Prices are numbers in your own currency; leave the price empty for 'ask us'.
_help.faqs: One per line: question | answer. Keep answers to one or two sentences.
_help.payment.bank.name: The bank customers transfer to. Shown only when someone asks how to pay.
_help.payment.bank.number: The account number. This stays in your own profile.
_help.conversation.handoverKeywords: Words that make the assistant hand the chat to a human immediately, e.g. refund, manager, complaint.
_help.conversation.dailyMessageCap: How many messages one customer can get per day before the assistant stops replying to them.
_help.conversation.maxBotTurnsBeforeHuman: How many replies the assistant may send in one conversation before a human takes over.
_help.intake.fields: What the assistant must find out, e.g. name, area, budget. Up to twelve fields.
_help.replyTiming: 'natural' (typing delay like a person), 'instant', or 'business hours only'.
_help.documents: A menu, price list or policy as PDF, DOCX, TXT or CSV, up to 5 MB. The assistant quotes from it.
_help.decisions: Set up the decision team with .team add Name 92300… payments,chat, then .chain payment owner:0,92300…:15. The AI never accepts or rejects a payment; a person does.

owner._help: EXAMPLE SECTION — every value here is a placeholder, not a real person. Replace them with your own. name and brand are what the bot says when a customer asks who they are talking to; location and timezone decide when it may promise a reply. services, addons, process and payment are the only prices and payment facts it may quote. team = people the bot can hand a chat to; friends = people who skip the sales script. Write numbers as country code + number, no plus sign and no spaces: 923001234567.
owner.name: Your Name
owner.responsePromise: usually replies within a few hours
owner.bio: I build websites, mobile apps, dashboards, AI bots and automation for small businesses. I work solo, so you always talk to the person writing the code — no account managers, no hand-offs.
skills: AI agents, chatbots & LLM integrations (OpenAI, Groq, Gemini)
process: You tell me the goal and features in chat
I send a fixed scope + price (no surprise bills)
50% advance to book the slot, 50% on delivery
You get a staging link and weekly progress updates
Delivery with 2 weeks of free bug fixes

payment.terms: 50% advance, 50% on delivery. For projects above 100,000 PKR I can split into 3 milestones.

policies.revisions: Two rounds of revisions are included in every package; extra rounds are billed hourly.
policies.support: 2 weeks of free bug fixes after delivery. New features are quoted separately.
policies.ownership: You own the code and all accounts after final payment.
policies.refund: Advance is refundable minus work already done, if the project is cancelled in the first week.
policies.nda: Happy to sign an NDA — send it over and I'll review.
policies.timeline: Timelines start after the advance and after you provide content/assets.

faqs.a: Send me the goal, the main features and your timeline. I'll reply with a fixed scope and price, then we start after the advance.

faqs.q: Do you work with international clients?
faqs.a: Yes — most of my work is for clients in the UK, US, UAE and Saudi Arabia. I invoice in USD/GBP/AED too and I keep calls inside your timezone.

faqs.q: How do I pay from abroad?
faqs.a: Wise, Payoneer or USDT. I can also invoice in USD, GBP or AED.

faqs.q: Do you provide the content and images?
faqs.a: I can write the copy and source stock media, or you provide it — either works, it just changes the timeline slightly.

faqs.q: What if I need changes after delivery?
faqs.a: Two revision rounds are included. After that, small changes are billed hourly or covered by a monthly maintenance plan.

doNotSay: Never claim to have signed a contract or to have received a payment.
Never promise a delivery date before the advance is paid.
Never give a final price above the configured ranges without asking the owner.
Never share the owner's personal address or phone number with strangers.

bot._help: EXAMPLE SECTION — the assistant, not you. name is what it calls itself; persona is the style instruction sent to the model with every reply. Keep persona to two or three sentences.
bot.name: Your Assistant
bot.persona: Warm, sharp, slightly informal. You talk like a busy but friendly human on WhatsApp — short messages, natural rhythm, no corporate script. You never sound like a chatbot or a call-centre.
bot.disclosure: You are the owner's AI assistant. Never claim to be a human, but keep it light: if someone asks whether you are a bot, say yes — you are the owner's assistant and can pass anything on to them.

business._help: EXAMPLE SECTION — your business profile. name, type, city and hours are quoted to customers, so keep them short and true; hours is free text, e.g. Daily 12:00-23:00. Anything you leave empty is never mentioned, and the bot will not invent it.
business.//: Universal profile (Phase 1). Used only when features.businessProfile is true. Fill it from scripts/tenant.js setup, a template, or .set from WhatsApp.

review.//: Hours to wait after .done before asking for feedback. 24 by default.

referral.//: Code tracking works with this empty. Set reward to promise something.

analyst.//: Weekly report for the owner, in this timezone.

payment._help: EXAMPLE SECTION — payment details. Only the fields you fill in are ever sent to a customer; empty ones are never invented. Write account numbers as plain digits, e.g. 03001234567.
payment.//: Only what is filled in is ever mentioned to a customer.

policies.//: maxDiscountPercent is the only discount the closer may offer. Remove it and every discount request goes to you.

invoice.//: PDF quotes/invoices. logo is a path inside this folder (PNG or JPG). footer replaces the default line.

crm.//: vipSpend: a customer who has spent this much (in business.currency) becomes vip automatically.

orderMessages.//: Edit freely. Placeholders: {first_name} {name} {id} {status} {total} {eta} {business}. Any status you leave out falls back to the built-in line in the customer's language.

orderReminders.//: Hours an unpaid order waits before each polite reminder. Env ORDER_REMINDER_HOURS / ORDER_REMINDER_SECOND_HOURS win over these.

catalog._help: EXAMPLE SECTION — what you sell. Each item needs a name and a price (or min/max), plus the keywords a customer would actually type. Leave items empty if you do not sell from a list.
catalog.//: The price list the bot may quote. Each item: { name, kind: service|product, price OR min/max, duration (minutes), stock, keywords }.

tone.//: Free-form house style. Example: { style, emoji, address, avoid }.
tone.//maxSentences: How long a normal reply may be (quotes and lists are exempt). Default 2.
tone.//humanTouch: Reactions for ok/thanks, no self-descriptions, an honest answer to 'am I a bot?'. Default on; the honest answer cannot be switched off.
tone.//replyTiming: How long a reply may take and how it feels while it is written. Env vars override these.

replyTiming.//: Milliseconds. 5-15 s from the customer message to the reply.

goals.//: What the bot should push these chats toward.

_agentsHelp: EXAMPLE SECTION — custom named assistants. Empty means the built-in assistant answers everything. Each agent needs an id, a name and a role (sales, support, booking, orders or custom); instructions are capped at 400 characters and are checked for prompt injection when you save them. tools may only narrow what the tenant already allows — an agent can never gain a tool you have not switched on. hours is free text, e.g. 09:00-18:00; outside them the next suitable agent answers. handoff is a team member name or "owner". Switch the feature on with features.multiAgent, then use .agents in WhatsApp.

agents.name: Sales Assistant
agents.instructions: Answer price questions from the catalogue, qualify the goal and the budget, then offer a quote. Never invent a price.

escalation.//: When and how to hand over to a human.

features._help: EXAMPLE SECTION — optional capabilities. true switches one on, false leaves it off, and anything omitted keeps its default. Nothing here needs a value beyond true or false.
features.//: Every new capability is opt-in and false by default. See README > Feature flags.
features.//aliases: closer / reviews / analyst still work — they map to closerAgent / reviewAgent / analystAgent.
features.//orders: order lifecycle and the mini CRM are opt-in too: .set features.orderTracking true
features.//marketing: the marketing team is owner-facing drafts: .marketing to see it
features.//brain: the business brain reads your own numbers and proposes; it never sends on its own: .brain to see it

_brainHelp: EXAMPLE SECTION — the business brain reads this. minutesPerConversation feeds the 'time saved' figure. thinDataConversations is the point below which it says 'not enough data'. dailyReasoningCalls caps how many reasoning-model calls one tenant may make per day. autoRun lists action types the brain may run without asking (leave empty unless you mean it).

brain._autoRunHelp: Possible values: followup, quote_reminder, offer, upsell, review_ask, reactivate. Anything listed still respects caps, opt-outs and quiet hours.

_marketingHelp: EXAMPLE SECTION — the marketing team reads this. approvalMode true means every promo waits for you. events are your own dates: [{"name": "Shop anniversary", "date": "2026-03-01"}]. channels are where your posters/QRs live: ["Instagram", "shop window"].

marketing._maxDiscountHelp: Add policies.maxDiscountPercent to your owner.json (e.g. 15) to let the offer checker approve small discounts. Without it, every discount is your decision.
